issues.issue: Lender must give the Plan-assets notice "upon the execution of this Agreement or upon initiation of such Loan under Section 2.1," without saying which occasion controls or what follows if neither notice is given. The trigger for conducting a Loan under PTE 81-6 is therefore uncertain.

The representation flips to Lender if Lender "fails to communicate and keep current" Plan information, with no standard for currency, no deadline, and no materiality qualifier. When the shift occurs is left to argument.

Section 17.3 requires daily marking "pursuant to Section 9.7," and there is no Section 9.7 in the Agreement — Section 9 ends at 9.6, and the Customer mark-to-market rule is Section 9.1. The obligation points to a provision that does not exist.

Section 17.4(c) lets Lender terminate "at any time" with delivery within a period measured from the customary delivery cycle or five Business Days, which cannot be squared with Section 6.1(a)'s termination-date regime keyed to the standard settlement date on notice. Which timetable governs a PTE 81-6 Loan is unresolved.

Section 18 makes all Loans a single agreement with cross-default and cross-Loan setoff, while Annex I-A ¶4 provides that the portion of each Loan allocable to each Principal is a separate agreement with that Principal. Cross-Loan netting against a multi-principal Agent cannot be given effect under both.

This Agreement is governed by New York law, while the Securities Lending Agreement under which Wells Fargo lends the same securities as agent is governed by Minnesota law. Which law governs the collateral and risk-of-loss questions arising from a single lending transaction is not settled by either clause.

The last sentence requires a writing only for "waivers in respect of a Default," leaving waivers of every other term to be established without a writing despite the opening non-waiver sentence. The two sentences set different rules for different waivers with no stated boundary.

Section 21 makes all remedies and obligations survive termination of the Agreement, while Section 24.1 says termination is "subject only to fulfillment of any obligations then outstanding." What survives a notice of termination cannot be read from either alone.

A notice is "deemed effective" when received or, if not received, when "delivery was in good faith attempted," so an undelivered demand can start margin and cure clocks. "Good faith attempted" is given no evidentiary content.

Jurisdiction is submitted to "SOLELY FOR THE PURPOSE OF" enforcement proceedings, yet the same sentence extends to any proceeding "RELATING IN ANY WAY TO THIS AGREEMENT." The limiting word and the expansive words describe different scopes.

The supersession clause is itself subject to whatever "the parties" may otherwise agree, with no requirement of writing, while the later sentence of Section 24.1 permits modification only by a signed writing. Whether an unwritten side understanding survives supersession is unresolved.

The bar on assignment without consent does not say whether an Agent's substitution or reallocation of Principals under Annex I-A is an assignment of the Agreement. Annex I-A contemplates changes of Principal without Borrower's consent to the Agreement itself.

Termination on notice is "subject only to fulfillment of any obligations then outstanding," which cannot be squared with Section 21's provision that all remedies and Loan obligations survive termination of the Agreement. The two describe different post-termination positions.

Modification is permitted only by a signed writing, yet Section 24.2 expressly allows agreements under Sections 10.5(b) and 25.37 to be made orally, and dozens of operative provisions apply only "unless otherwise agreed" without requiring a writing. Whether an oral variation of a Loan term is effective turns on which sentence prevails.

"Time is of the essence" for each Loan cannot be squared with Sections 12.4 and 12.8, which make a failure to transfer or pay a Default only after notice and a cure period running to the next day's Cutoff Time. Whether a late transfer is instantly actionable is left in doubt.

Treating "each provision and agreement herein ... as separate and independent from any other provision" sits against Section 18, by which all Loans constitute a single agreement entered into in consideration of one another. The severability sentence, read literally, would undo the single-agreement premise.

The sentence opens "Any 4 between Borrower and Lender pursuant to Section 10.5(b) or Section 25.37," omitting the noun (agreement) that the formal requirements attach to. What class of dealings must satisfy clauses (a)–(c) cannot be read from the words.

An Act of Insolvency includes the appointment of an official for "any substantial part of its property," with no measure of substantiality. Since the consequence is automatic termination of all Loans, the boundary of the term matters.

The definition sweeps in any broker or dealer "regardless of whether the activities of such person are conducted in the United States or otherwise require such person to register," so a bank with dealer-type activities may qualify. Because Section 4.2 excuses a Broker-Dealer Lender from segregating Collateral and lets it Retransfer, the breadth of this definition decides those duties.

A Business Day is a day on which regular trading occurs "in the principal market" for the relevant Securities, a market the Agreement never identifies for any Loan. Deadlines throughout Sections 6, 9 and 12 depend on that unidentified market.

The definition assigns "Cash Collateral Fee" the meaning given in "Section 3.1," but Section 3.1 concerns the transfer of Loaned Securities; the term is defined in Section 5.1. The cross-reference points to the wrong provision.

"Close of Business" is whatever the parties agree in Schedule B "or otherwise orally or in writing" and, failing that, is "determined in accordance with market practice"; the executed Schedule B fixes no time. A deadline used throughout Sections 4, 6, 9 and 12 is left to unwritten practice.

"Collateral" is defined to include the accounts in which cash collateral is deposited, the securities in which it is "invested or reinvested," and the proceeds of both, yet Sections 4.3 and 6.2 simply require "the Collateral" to be returned on termination. Whether Borrower is owed its cash back or only the reinvestment assets at their then value is the product of reading the definition against those return obligations.

"Customer" is defined by reference to Rule 15c3-3 status "to the extent that Borrower is subject to such Rule," so whether a given Lender is a Customer depends on an unstated regulatory characterization. Sections 3.2, 9.1 and 25.11 all switch on that status.

"Cutoff Time" is left to agreement "in Schedule B or otherwise orally or in writing" and, in the absence of agreement, to "market practice," and Schedule B fixes no such time. Every delivery deadline in Sections 3, 4, 6 and 12 rests on this undetermined hour.

"Distribution" is defined as any distribution "including, but not limited to" six enumerated categories, leaving the general words to be measured against the specifics. Whether items such as merger consideration or corporate-action proceeds are Distributions or instead substituted Loaned Securities under Section 25.33 is left open.

"Equity Security" is defined negatively as any security other than a "nonequity security" as defined in Regulation T, so its content depends entirely on a regulation "as in effect from time to time." Whether a given instrument is an Equity Security — which decides the Annex III Term Loan default rule — cannot be read from the Agreement.

The rate is the published rate "on that day," but the definition never says which day is meant — the date of purchase, of sale, or each day of accrual. Sections 13.1 and 13.2 apply the rate "as such rate fluctuates from day to day," leaving the reference ambiguous.

"Foreign Securities" are those "principally cleared and settled outside the United States," with no test for what makes clearing and settlement principal. The default interest rate under Sections 13.1–13.2 and the settlement date under Schedule B ¶3 both turn on this word.
